hartlib.lead: Hartlib is one research chat over everything you subscribe to, for people who read professional briefings.
points: Answers plain-language questions with each claim linked to its page
Reads dense briefings, letters and official records for you
Lets publishers publish issues and invite client companies

silo.lead: Silo gives each AI agent its own Linux or macOS virtual machine, for apps that run agents on your Mac.
points: Lets agents use credentials without being able to read them
Limits GitHub access to repositories you pick, read-only by default
Saves checkpoints so you can restore or copy a computer

lcu.lead: LCU lets AI agents in tools like Claude Code or Pi control your desktop apps, using Codex's own engine.
points: Reads and controls Chrome tabs, with approval for each site
Asks you to approve each app before the agent can touch it
Manages the list of always-allowed apps from the terminal with Touch ID

fjord.lead: Fjord sits between your Claude Code sessions and GitHub, and brings you only what you need to know or decide.
points: Answer every Claude Code session's questions and plans from one page
Sort your GitHub inbox and CI by rules you write as sentences
Hand a failing check to the Claude Code session that can fix it

sic.lead: Sic checks the facts in French political debates against official sources, live or on replay.
points: Turns debate audio into text and names who is speaking
Picks out checkable claims and skips opinions and promises
Gives no verdict without a cited source and a precise link

lastdrop.lead: lastdrop lets Claude Code call any model as its own subagent, for people with several AI accounts.
points: Switches to the next model when one is out of quota or can't start
Runs Claude's subagents on your other Claude accounts
Shows usage left and reset times for each account in the menu bar
